doc.headline: No bar declared, so the pick is a price. Lean: Brisk-S, low reasoning, retry. Atlas-M's best is not told apart from Brisk-S at high reasoning, yet costs {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.multiple} as much at this run's routing
doc.lede: Brisk-S at low reasoning with retry trails Atlas-M's best by {compare.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.difference|abs} points; on point estimates, the next point past it costs about {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a month. A declared bar or price per point from the planner's owner would turn this into a decision.

caveats.material_if: The high covers, at this run's routing, the frontier's shape, the price per point rising at every step, and Atlas-M's premium over Brisk-S at matched reasoning; it does not cover the lean, which stays open until the owner declares a bar or a price per point. The lean is cheapest only for a price between {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} and {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a month on point estimates, and that upper edge rests on a gain of {compare.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.difference} points ({compare.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval})

Only if the owner needs the move from today's planner. Every option here is a candidate, so choosing among them needs no control; no configuration is marked as the one in production, so nothing here reads a change from it

Fresh cases read the lean's lead over Nano-XS at high reasoning with retry near zero; that lead's interval is {compare.brisk-s.low.r1.nano-xs.high.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval}, and the best of many configurations tends to read lower on a re-run, which the paired re-run checks

caveats.label: Cost routing and volume unit unknown
caveats.material_if: Another provider routing changes the models' prices per call relative to each other, or the declared monthly volume counts tasks rather than calls. The snapshot names no provider for any configuration. Atlas-M's premium over Brisk-S is {cost.gap.atlas-m.low.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.multiple} at low reasoning and {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.multiple} at high, so a re-routing would have to cut Atlas-M's price relative to Brisk-S's by about that factor to close it; the price edges between nearer options could move with far smaller shifts. If the volume counts tasks and a call is a tool call, each monthly cost scales by its calls per task ({measure.calls_per_task.brisk-s.low.r1.mean} for the lean, {measure.calls_per_task.atlas-m.high.r1.mean} for Atlas-M at high reasoning with retry, {measure.calls_per_task.nano-xs.high.r1.mean} for Nano-XS at high reasoning with retry), which raises every price edge by about that factor and moves the lean's band up; no figure states the per-task prices

decision.text: Atlas-M at high reasoning with retry passes {compare.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.difference|abs} points more than Brisk-S at low reasoning with retry ({compare.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval}), for {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.monthly|abs} more a month at the declared volume, read as calls, at this run's routing. Brisk-S at high reasoning with retry is not told apart from Atlas-M on pass rate at {cost_per_1k.brisk-s.high.r1} per 1k calls against {cost_per_1k.atlas-m.high.r1}. Nothing declared before the run ranks cost against pass rate; the planner's owner makes the call.

By price per point a month, on point estimates: below {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point}, a Nano-XS configuration; up to {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point}, Brisk-S at low reasoning with retry; up to {price.brisk-s.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point}, Brisk-S at high reasoning with retry; above it, Atlas-M at high reasoning with retry. These edges carry no interval, and both upper steps rest on gains not told apart from zero.

Ours, not a rule: Brisk-S at low reasoning with retry, at {cost_per_1k.brisk-s.low.r1} per 1k calls. It holds for a price per point between {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} and {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a month.

The next step up, Brisk-S at high reasoning with retry, gains {compare.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.difference|abs} points on the lean, not told apart from zero ({compare.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval}); a fresh run of today's size reads it the other way {settle.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.wrong_side} of the time. At the top of that interval the price of a point falls well below the lean's upper edge, so the band is soft. The lean is the best of {n_candidates|words} configurations near its price, so its rate may read lower on fresh cases.

A pass-rate bar or a price per point, declared by the planner's owner, with the unit the monthly volume counts. Then a paired re-run of the two Brisk-S options with retry settles whether high reasoning's gain is real.

claims.text: Along the cost frontier of the {n_candidates|words} configurations, pass rate climbs steeply across the cheapest and flattens past Brisk-S at low reasoning with retry, at {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.mean}.

evidence.caption: The {count.frontier.pass_rate|words} configurations on the frontier, cost per 1k calls on a log axis against pass rate, the lean stressed; every other configuration is in the full results.

claims.text: The price of a pass-rate point rises at every step along the frontier, reaching {price.brisk-s.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a month for the last step to Atlas-M.

evidence.caption: Monthly price of each pass-rate point gained along the frontier, at the declared volume read as calls and this run's routing; point estimates with no interval.

claims.text: At this run's unnamed provider routing, Atlas-M costs {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.multiple} as much as Brisk-S at the same reasoning level with retry, yet the two are not told apart on pass rate ({lever.model.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.interval} at high reasoning).

evidence.caption: Change in pass rate from switching Atlas-M to Brisk-S, or low to high reasoning, all with retry; unpaired intervals.
Cost per 1k calls for the same four configurations, on a log scale.

claims.text: Retry buys most where pass rate starts lowest: on Brisk-S at low reasoning it adds {lever.retry.brisk-s.low.r0.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.effect} points for {cost.gap.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.low.r0.per_1k|abs} more per 1k calls, with calls per task moving from {measure.calls_per_task.brisk-s.low.r0.mean} to {measure.calls_per_task.brisk-s.low.r1.mean}; it adds more on Nano-XS, and on Atlas-M at high reasoning a gain not told apart from zero.

evidence.caption: Change in pass rate from adding retry to each shortlisted option, beside the Atlas-M to Nano-XS gap with and without retry; unpaired intervals.
Cost per 1k calls without and with retry for the same three options, on a log scale.

claims.text: Atlas-M at high reasoning with retry is the slowest option on the shortlist, its p95 latency at {measure.latency_ms.atlas-m.high.r1.p95}; no latency budget was declared, and retry lengthens the tail.

evidence.caption: Latency from p50 to p95 for the options a decider would weigh.

claims.text: Multi-hop questions are the weakest task for every shortlisted option; the lean passes {task.multihop.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean} of them. With no per-task counts this is a lead, not a separated finding.

evidence.caption: Pass rate by task for the shortlisted options; point estimates.
The failures kept for the lean, one per task shown; the multi-hop card collapses two hops into one query. Illustrations, not a count.

If the volume counts tasks, each edge rises by about the configurations' calls per task.

method.text: {n_candidates|words} configurations: three models crossed with three reasoning levels and retry on or off. With retry means {settings.brisk-s.low.r1.retry} retry.
{scoreboard.brisk-s.low.r1.cases} cases per configuration, none lost; repeats are not stated, nor whether every configuration ran the same cases.
The input does not define what makes a task pass; failed cases are classed as missing call, wrong arguments or wrong tool.

At {lever.model.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.level}, from each rate's binomial spread over its cases, two configurations combined as independent, with no correction for the many comparisons. Where the configurations ran the same cases, a paired interval would be narrower. Task figures carry no counts and so no interval.
No configuration is marked as production; every comparison is between two configurations' own figures.

Cost per 1k calls as measured in this run; the provider routing is not named, and the input does not say whether a call is a planner request or a tool call. Monthly figures read the declared volume of {meta.volume_per_month} as calls, which the input does not state.
Median (p50) and p95 per configuration; no latency budget was declared.

findings.finding: The confidence clause on the pick being best of several says 'Fresh cases read the lean's lead over Nano-XS at high reasoning with retry near zero; that lead's interval is +0.8 to +4'. No fresh-case reading exists. The measured lead is +2.4 points (+0.8 to +4). A reader would think a re-run had erased the lean's edge over the option $764 a month cheaper. Rewrite it as a risk, not a result. For example: 'The lean's lead over Nano-XS at high reasoning with retry is +2.4 points (+0.8 to +4); as the best of eighteen, it may read lower on fresh cases, and the paired re-run checks it.'

'The price of a pass-rate point rises at every step along the frontier' is true by construction. The frontier here is the convex hull, so its steps always get dearer, and the confidence's High covering 'the price per point rising at every step' claims nothing the data could have refuted. Say the frontier is the price-per-point hull and that its steps rise by construction. Put the finding in the size of the steps, for example the jump from $1,595.18 to $17,236.36 for the last step to Atlas-M. Then drop 'rising at every step' from what the High covers. In the frontier claim's caption, note that Brisk-S at low reasoning without retry (95.3% at $0.288) is not beaten by any cheaper option but lies under the hull. It is the pick for a bar between 94.8% and 95.3%, as the bar row in 'What you could change' already says.

The examples caption says 'one per task shown', but there are three cards for four tasks and none for single lookup. The snapshot keeps only three failures for the lean. Say 'one per task for the three tasks with a kept failure', so a reader doesn't look for a missing single-lookup card.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline and lede say the decision is open because no pass-rate bar or price per point was declared. The decision block names the lean (Brisk-S at low reasoning with retry, $0.302 per 1k calls), the price band where it holds ($319.67 to $1,595.18 a month), and the next step it rests on (high reasoning on Brisk-S gains +0.8, -0.4 to +2.1). The frontier claim shows where pass rate flattens. A reader can say what is unresolved, why, and what to do next. The wording problems on this screen (the 'High' confidence, 'at least', '12 times') are scored under honest emphasis.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: I checked each claim against its own values table, row by row, and no block contradicts its sentence. In frontier, pass rate goes from 81.0% to 97.1% over the cheapest tenth of the cost range, then gains 1.5 points over an 11.5x cost rise. In price-steps, the price per point rises at every step: $3.20, $17.31, $111.22, $319.67, $1,595.18, $17,236.36. In atlas-premium, both Atlas-M vs Brisk-S rows include zero (-2.0 to +0.5 and -1.7 to +0.4). In retry, the gain shrinks as the starting rate rises: +3.4 from 91.3%, +1.9 from 95.3%, +0.9 from 97.7%. In multihop, multi-hop is the lowest task in all four columns. The tool reproduces the figures: +1.5 (+0.3 to +2.6), +2.4 (+0.8 to +4), 9.4% wrong side, 5,432 cases.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The lean's weak points are on the page. Watch says high reasoning's +0.8 gain over the lean is not told apart from zero, and the best-of-n caveat is there. But the confidence reads High over four open caveats. One of them (nothing declared) is the decision itself, and the lean's upper price edge rests on that unresolved +0.8 step. The lede says each point past the lean costs 'at least $1,595.18' when that is a point estimate on a gain whose interval crosses zero. The headline's '12 times' rounds up 11.5x ($3.477 vs $0.302).

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Leaving out Atlas-M at no and low reasoning is right. Each is beaten by a cheaper Brisk-S option, for example $1.655 at 97.9% against $0.633 at 98.0%. The calls-per-task omission is weaker. It says the shortlist order holds, which is true. But if the declared 4,000,000 counts tasks, every price edge rises about 1.5x and the lean's band becomes roughly $490 to $2,260. That changes the pick for an owner valuing a point at about $1,600 to $2,260 a month. The note also says Atlas-M's per-task cost sits 'further' away, but Atlas-M makes fewer calls per task (1.452 vs 1.539), so it sits closer.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: Each confound is carried somewhere. Unnamed provider routing and the unknown volume unit are a confidence caveat and a next step. Not knowing whether arms ran the same cases is in Method, the intervals are labelled unpaired, and the re-run is paired. The missing control and best-of-n optimism are both carried as caveats. The page addresses the cost_served_by fact by saying no provider is named for any configuration. Calls per task is handled under elision.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names an action and what it settles. The owner declares a bar or price, which turns the trade into a decision. A paired re-run of the two Brisk-S retry options at 5,432 each settles high reasoning's gain four times in five and checks best-of-n optimism. A hop-collapsing prompt fix, re-run with stated counts, settles the weakest task. Recording the provider and the volume unit settles whether the monthly prices hold.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: The price-steps, retry, latency and multihop blocks each show their claim's own figures. Two blocks fall short. The frontier block plots all eighteen configurations but does not mark which seven are on the frontier, so the claim's 'seven of eighteen' cannot be read from it. The atlas-premium block shows the pass-rate gaps but not the costs behind '5.5 times as much' ($1.655 vs $0.302, $3.477 vs $0.633), so half of that claim is not in its evidence.

findings.finding: The confidence reads 'High, if the caveats below aren't material' over four open caveats, and at least one is plausibly material. The nothing-declared caveat is the decision itself. The lean's upper edge ($1,595.18) rests on a +0.8 gain whose interval is -0.4 to +2.1, which a run of today's size reads the wrong way 9.4% of the time. The best-of-n and routing caveats do not say why the call holds until they are resolved. Fix: say what the High covers (the frontier's shape, the rising price per point, Atlas-M's premium over Brisk-S at the same reasoning level) and that the lean itself stays open until the owner declares a price or bar. Otherwise make the confidence low.

The lede says each point past the lean 'costs at least $1,595.18 a month'. That figure is a point estimate on a +0.8 gain (-0.4 to +2.1). At the top of that interval the price would be about $630 a point. Write 'about $1,595.18, on point estimates', as the decision block already says. In the headline, '12 times the cost' is 11.5x ($3.477 vs $0.302); print the multiple as computed.

The headline frames the trade as Atlas-M at high reasoning with retry against the lean. But Atlas-M's lead over Brisk-S at high reasoning with retry is not told apart from zero (atlas-premium: -1.7 to +0.4), and that Brisk-S option costs $0.633, about a fifth of Atlas-M's $3.477. Name the lean in the headline and say the top pass rate is matched, within its interval, at a fifth of Atlas-M's price. Otherwise a first-screen reader takes Atlas-M as the quality ceiling.

The monthly prices count the declared 4,000,000 as calls. If it counts tasks, every cost scales by calls per task: about 1.54 for the lean, 1.48 for Brisk-S at high reasoning with retry, 1.57 for Nano-XS at high reasoning with retry, 1.45 for Atlas-M. The lean's band then moves from $319.67–$1,595.18 to roughly $490–$2,260, and the last step to Atlas-M from $17,236 to about $24,900. Put these per-task edges in the volume-unit caveat or the Explore price row. Correct the omitted note: Atlas-M makes fewer calls per task, so its per-task cost sits closer to the others, not further. In the retry claim, '$0.014 more per 1k calls' likewise understates retry's cost per task, because retry adds calls (1.492 to 1.539).

The claim says seven of the eighteen configurations are on the frontier, but the scatter's table marks only the lean. Mark the seven frontier points (Nano-XS off with and without retry, Nano-XS low with retry, Nano-XS high with retry, the lean, Brisk-S high with retry, Atlas-M high with retry), or draw the frontier line, so a reader can see where pass rate flattens.

The claim says Atlas-M 'costs 5.5 times as much', but the block shows only pass-rate gaps. Add the cost-per-1k pairs ($1.655 vs $0.302 at low reasoning, $3.477 vs $0.633 at high) so the premium shows in the block. This claim ranks two models by cost, and the snapshot names no provider for any of them, so add 'at this run's unnamed provider routing' to the claim. As written, the multiple reads as a property of the models.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline now names the lean (Brisk-S at low reasoning with retry). It says plainly that no bar was declared, so the pick comes down to a price. It also says Atlas-M's best is not told apart from Brisk-S at high reasoning with retry. The decision block gives the price bands. Watch gives the main risk: the next step up gains +0.8 points (-0.4 to +2.1), and a fresh run reads it the other way 9.4% of the time. The first claim (frontier) shows where pass rate flattens. This resolves last round's headline and lede findings: the cost multiple is 5.5x as computed, and the lede says 'about $1,595.18' on point estimates. The headline's cost multiple has no routing qualifier; that is raised under the confidence finding.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: I checked each claim against its block's rows. In frontier, the gains run 7.5, 4.2, 2.0, 2.4, 0.8 and 0.7 points, so the curve flattens past the lean at 97.1%. In price-steps, $3.20, $17.31, $111.22, $319.67, $1,595.18 and $17,236.36 rise at every step; price_tradeoff gives the same frontier of seven and the same edges. In atlas-premium, both model rows straddle zero, and the cost bars show about 5.5x at both reasoning levels. In retry, the gains of +0.9, +1.9 and +3.4 sort by starting rate (97.7%, 95.3%, 91.3%). In multihop, multi-hop is the lowest of the four tasks in every shortlisted row. In latency, Atlas-M at high reasoning with retry is the longest at 2551 ms, and retry raises p95 from 465 to 513 ms. No row contradicts its sentence.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The lean's weak axes are visible. The step above it is not told apart from zero, its band is soft at the top of that interval, and it is the best of eighteen configurations. The confidence now scopes the High away from the lean. But it says the High covers 'Atlas-M's premium over Brisk-S at matched reasoning' and the rising price per point. Both are cost figures read at a provider routing the snapshot does not name, and the page's own routing caveat says another routing could reorder them. The High stands behind exactly what that open caveat could move. The headline's '5.5 times as much' also carries no routing qualifier.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Every omitted Atlas-M configuration at no or low reasoning is beaten by a cheaper Brisk-S configuration that passes at least as often: $1.000 at 94.0% against $0.288 at 95.3%, and $1.655 at 97.9% against $0.633 at 98.0%. The calls-per-task note is now corrected (Atlas-M's premium shrinks per task), and its effect on the price edges is carried in the confidence. The outcome and extra-calls measures have no figures in the snapshot. None of the omissions would change the call.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: The volume unit is now carried with calls per task for each option: 1.539 for the lean, 1.452 for Atlas-M and 1.566 for Nano-XS. This resolves last round's price-steps finding. Best-of-many is carried into Watch and into the paired re-run. Unknown routing is carried into a next step (record each configuration's provider). But the confidence clause names routing as a condition without saying why the covered cost findings hold until it is resolved. The no-control clause likewise does not say why the call holds without a control.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names an action and what it settles. The owner declares a bar or a price per point, plus the volume unit. A paired re-run of the two Brisk-S options with retry, at 5,432 cases each, has 80% power at today's +0.8 gap; the unpaired arithmetic checks out, so it is conservative for a paired run. A hop-collapsing fix on multi-hop is re-run with stated counts. Recording each configuration's provider checks whether the premium holds at production routing.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: Last round's block findings are resolved. The frontier scatter now lists exactly the seven frontier points. atlas-premium now carries the cost bars and the routing qualifier. One gap remains. The retry claim's cost figures, '$0.014 more per 1k calls and a few more calls per task', are not in its block, which shows only pass-rate gaps. 'A few more calls per task' also overstates the change: the snapshot gives 1.492 to 1.539, which is +0.047 calls per task. Otherwise the blocks pass the counterfactual: if the multi-hop rows reordered, or the model intervals excluded zero, the claims would have to change.

findings.finding: The confidence's first clause says the High covers 'the price per point rising at every step, and Atlas-M's premium over Brisk-S at matched reasoning'. Both are cost readings at a provider routing the snapshot never names (cost_served_by: no configuration's pricing is stated). The fourth clause concedes that 'another provider routing reorders the costs per 1k calls', but it does not say why the covered findings hold until the routing is known. The headline also ranks Atlas-M against Brisk-S by cost ('costs 5.5 times as much') with no routing named. Fix: say the High on these findings holds 'at this run's routing'. Then either say why routing is unlikely to undo them (for example, the premium is about 5.5x at both reasoning levels, $1.655 vs $0.302 and $3.477 vs $0.633, so a re-routing would have to cut Atlas-M's price per call relative to Brisk-S's by more than five times to close it) or leave them outside the High. Add 'at this run's routing' to the headline's 5.5x. While there, give the no-control clause its reason the call holds (every option here is a candidate, so the choice among them does not need a control; only the move from today's planner does). Fix the lowercase sentence starts ('. the high covers', '. the owner needs').

The claim says retry on Brisk-S at low reasoning adds '+1.9 points for $0.014 more per 1k calls and a few more calls per task'. The snapshot gives calls per task of 1.492 without retry and 1.539 with it, so retry adds 0.047 calls per task, about 3%, not 'a few'. Neither cost figure is in the block, which draws only pass-rate gaps. Replace 'a few more calls per task' with '+0.047 calls per task (1.492 to 1.539)', and add the cost per 1k pair ($0.288 vs $0.302) as a small bars block or a values row. That way the cost side of the retry trade shows next to its gain.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, lede and decision block make three things clear. No bar was declared, so the choice is a price. The lean is Brisk-S at low reasoning with retry, and it holds for a price per point between $319.67 and $1,595.18 a month. Atlas-M at high reasoning with retry costs 5.5 times as much as Brisk-S at high reasoning, now stated as at this run's routing, and the two are not told apart on pass rate. The main risk is in Watch: Brisk-S at high reasoning gains +0.8 points (-0.4 to +2.1) on the lean, a gain not told apart from zero. The frontier claim shows where the curve flattens.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: I checked each claim against its table and found no contradictions. The trade is +1.5 points (+0.3 to +2.6) for $12,700 a month, which matches (3.477-0.302)×4,000. The price edges $319.67, $1,595.18 and $17,236.36 match price_tradeoff. Multi-hop is the lowest task in all four shortlisted rows (93.5, 95.6, 97.3, 97.9). In the retry claim, the gains fall as the starting rate rises (+3.4, +1.9, +0.9), as the claim says. The one broken sentence is in the confidence block, not in a claim, and is raised under Honest emphasis.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The lean's weak axes are visible: the soft upper edge, best-of-many optimism, multi-hop as its weakest task, and the routing and volume-unit caveats. But the best-of-many clause says 'Fresh cases read the lean's lead over Nano-XS at high reasoning with retry near zero'. No fresh cases were run, and the measured lead is +2.4 points (+0.8 to +4). As written, the clause reports a re-run finding that does not exist, and that finding would wipe out the reason to pay $764 a month over Nano-XS.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Nothing omitted changes the call. Atlas-M at no or low reasoning is beaten by Brisk-S at high reasoning, which costs less and passes as often (Atlas-M low with retry: 97.9% at $1.655; Brisk-S high with retry: 98.0% at $0.633). Per task, the order holds: Atlas-M high with retry is about $5.05 per 1k tasks against $0.93 for Brisk-S high with retry and $0.47 for the lean. The other omissions have no data behind them or sit in the appendix.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: Each confound is carried into the story and the next steps: the unnamed provider routing (the 5.5x factor a re-routing would have to overcome), the unstated volume unit (calls per task given for each option), no control (explained as not needed to choose among candidates), unpaired intervals (in Method), and best-of-many (the paired re-run).

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names an action and what it settles. The owner declares a bar or a price per point and the volume unit. A paired re-run of the two Brisk-S options with retry, at 5,432 cases each, settles high reasoning's gain with 80% power and checks the lean against optimism. A multi-hop prompt fix is re-run with case counts. Recording each provider settles the routing question.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: Most blocks fit. The Atlas-M premium and retry claims now show cost bars beside the pass-rate gaps. The retry claim gives calls per task as 1.492 to 1.539, which resolves my earlier should_fix. The price-steps claim fails the counterfactual. Its 'frontier' is the convex hull that price_tradeoff draws, and on a hull the price per point rises at every step by construction. So no data could break the claim, and the confidence's High covering it adds nothing. The hull also leaves out Brisk-S at low reasoning without retry (95.3% at $0.288). No cheaper option passes as often, and the bar row in 'What you could change' names it as the pick for a bar between 94.8% and 95.3%.

findings.finding: The confidence clause on the pick being best of several says 'Fresh cases read the lean's lead over Nano-XS at high reasoning with retry near zero; that lead's interval is +0.8 to +4'. No fresh-case reading exists. The measured lead is +2.4 points (+0.8 to +4). A reader would think a re-run had erased the lean's edge over the option $764 a month cheaper. Rewrite it as a risk, not a result. For example: 'The lean's lead over Nano-XS at high reasoning with retry is +2.4 points (+0.8 to +4); as the best of eighteen, it may read lower on fresh cases, and the paired re-run checks it.'

'The price of a pass-rate point rises at every step along the frontier' is true by construction. The frontier here is the convex hull, so its steps always get dearer, and the confidence's High covering 'the price per point rising at every step' claims nothing the data could have refuted. Say the frontier is the price-per-point hull and that its steps rise by construction. Put the finding in the size of the steps, for example the jump from $1,595.18 to $17,236.36 for the last step to Atlas-M. Then drop 'rising at every step' from what the High covers. In the frontier claim's caption, note that Brisk-S at low reasoning without retry (95.3% at $0.288) is not beaten by any cheaper option but lies under the hull. It is the pick for a bar between 94.8% and 95.3%, as the bar row in 'What you could change' already says.

The examples caption says 'one per task shown', but there are three cards for four tasks and none for single lookup. The snapshot keeps only three failures for the lean. Say 'one per task for the three tasks with a kept failure', so a reader doesn't look for a missing single-lookup card.
